answer: Each agent must post a bond locked in a smart contract before it can submit jobs or claim rewards; a challenge period lets peers expose duplicate identities by linking their deposits to the same controlling key. Proven duplicates forfeit their bonds, which are redistributed to challengers, so inventing identities requires tying up real capital and risks losing it. The cipher commits to each claim, while quartz and walnut serve as ordinary job labels, not proof of personhood.
